reports.title: Workday Announces Fiscal 2027 Third Quarter Financial Results

guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: Workday is providing guidance for the fiscal 2027 fourth quarter ending January 31, 2027 as follows:
•Subscription revenues of $2.600 billion, representing growth of 10%
Workday is updating guidance for the fiscal 2027 full year ending January 31, 2027 as follows:
•Subscription revenues of $9.958 billion, representing growth of 13%

desk.headline: Revenue up 11.2% to $2.71bn and adjusted EPS of $2.82, both above estimates; full-year outlook raised, Q4 subscription guide slightly below
results: Revenue rose 11.2% to $2.71bn, a little above the $2.69bn estimate; adjusted EPS of $2.82 beat the $2.74 estimate.
Subscription revenue grew 12.8% to $2.53bn, while professional services revenue fell to $173m from $188m.
The adjusted operating margin widened to 31.4% from 28.5%; GAAP EPS of $0.96 included $0.21 of restructuring costs.
Twelve-month subscription backlog rose 12.3% to $9.22bn; the total backlog grew 6.1% to $27.5bn.
Free cash flow was $691m and Workday bought back about 3.8m shares for $750m.

guidance.summary: Workday raised its full-year subscription revenue forecast to $9.958bn (13% growth) and its adjusted margin to 31.5%. Q4 subscription revenue of $2.60bn (10% growth) is slightly below what analysts expected.

points: Artificial-intelligence products brought in nearly $150m of new annual contract value, over three times a year ago.
About 30% of customers now license at least one such product; management said pricing for usage-based products is still early.
Q3 backlog was lifted by early renewals that are not expected to repeat in Q4, part of why Q4 growth slows.
For FY28, management pointed to about 11% subscription growth and an adjusted margin of at least 33%, with formal guidance next quarter.
International growth beat expectations, but US growth slowed; headcount should stay roughly flat.
call.source: Call coverage: Investing.com, 24 Nov 2026; SiliconANGLE, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Whether subscription growth steadies near 10–11% after the Q4 slowdown.
Formal FY28 guidance next quarter against the 11% growth and 33% margin pointers.
Slower US growth and how quickly usage-based products start adding revenue.
